rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage argues that only God can create and preserve hearing, sight, life, reason, and knowledge; therefore only God deserves worship, making idol worship false.
rows.anchor: القادر على تحصيل هذه القوى فيها وصونها عن الآفات والمخافات ليس إلا الله

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: The sealing of hearts means God stamped them so they could not understand guidance.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس : معناه وطبع على قلوبهم فلم يعقلوا الهدى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One reported interpretation takes sealing to mean removing their minds until they became like madmen.
rows.anchor: معناه وأزال عقولكم حتى تصيروا كالمجانين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another reported interpretation takes the sealing to mean causing their hearts to die.
rows.anchor: المراد بهذا الختم الاماتة أي يميت قلوبكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Grammatically, min is the nominative subject, ilāh its predicate, ghayr an adjective, and the pronoun in يأتيكم به refers to what the action removes.
rows.anchor: من } رفع بالابتداء وخبره { إله } و { غير } صفة له

rows.speaker: نافع
rows.claim: Nāfiʿ reads the pronoun in bihi with ḍamma, following a dialect that drops a connecting wāw when two sukūns meet; other readers use kasra.
rows.anchor: روي عن نافع { به انظر } بضم الهاء وهو على لغة من يقرأ

rows.speaker: حمزة والكسائي
rows.claim: Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī read yaṣdifūn with an imāla toward zāy; the others read it with ṣād, meaning they turn away.
rows.anchor: وقرأ حمزة والكسائي { يصدفون } باشمام الزاي والباقون بالصاد أي يعرضون عنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God presents signs in many forms so each reinforces the preceding proof; despite this unusually clear instruction, the addressees turn away.
rows.anchor: إيرادها على الوجوه المختلفة المتكاثرة بحث يكون كل واحد منها يقوي ما قبل

rows.speaker: الكعبي
rows.claim: Al-Kaʿbī argues that the verse shows God enabled people to understand and did not create their turning away; otherwise its reproach would make no sense.
rows.anchor: دلت هذه الآية على أنه تعالى مكنهم من الفهم ، ولم يخلق فيهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author answers that the verse more strongly supports his side: God made the proof fully clear, yet they persisted in unbelief, showing guidance and misguidance occur only through God's guidance and leading astray.
rows.anchor: وذلك يدل على أن الهدى والضلال لا يحصلان إلا بهداية الله وإلا بإضلاله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those signs points to the verses revealed in this surah, called al-Kitāb al-mubīn, the clear Book, meaning the Qur'an.
rows.anchor: إشارة إلى آيات هذه السورة أي تلك الآيات التي أنزلت إليك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur'an is clear because it is a decisive miracle and manifest sign for Muhammad.
rows.anchor: أن القرآن معجزة قاهرة وآية بينة لمحمد صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: It is clear because it sets out guidance, right conduct, lawful and unlawful matters.
rows.anchor: أنه بين فيه الهدى والرشد ، والحلال والحرام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: It is clear because it explains earlier peoples' stories and circumstances.
rows.anchor: أنه بينت فيه قصص الأولين وشرحت فيه أحوال المتقدمين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report says Jewish scholars told Meccan leaders to ask why Jacob's family moved from Syria to Egypt and about Joseph; the revelation uses Arabic so they could understand and learn.
rows.anchor: سلوا محمدا لم انتقل آل يعقوب من الشام إلى مصر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling this portion of revelation Qur'an is valid because Qur'an is a generic name that can denote the whole or a part.
rows.anchor: لأن القرآن اسم جنس يقع على الكل والبعض

rows.speaker: الجبائي
rows.claim: Al-Jubbāʾī argues that sending down implies change of state, so the Qur'an is created rather than eternal.
rows.anchor: فإن القديم لا يجوز تنزيله وإنزاله وتحويله من حال إلى حال

rows.speaker: الجبائي
rows.claim: Al-Jubbāʾī argues that being described as Arabic rules out the Qur'an's being eternal, since the eternal cannot be Arabic or Persian.
rows.anchor: أنه تعالى وصفه بكونه عربيا والقديم لا يكون عربيا ولا فارسيا

rows.speaker: الجبائي
rows.claim: Al-Jubbāʾī argues that God's ability to reveal it in a non-Arabic form shows it came into being.
rows.anchor: أنه تعالى كان قادرا على أن ينزله لا عربيا

rows.speaker: الجبائي
rows.claim: Al-Jubbāʾī argues that a book made of constituent verses and words is composite, and every composite thing is originated.
rows.anchor: يدل على أنه مركب من الآيات والكلمات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The arguments establish only that the arrangement of letters, words, and expressions is originated; the author says that is not the eternal reality he claims.
rows.anchor: تدل على أن المركب من الحروف والكلمات والألفاظ والعبارات محدث وذلك لا نزاع فيه

rows.speaker: الجبائي
rows.claim: Al-Jubbāʾī reads laʿallakum taʿqilūn as a definite purpose, not doubt, and infers that God intended all people to know monotheism and religion, against the determinists.
rows.anchor: يجب حملها على الجزم والتقدير : إنا أنزلناه قرآنا عربيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author grants that God intended them to learn this story from the surah, but says that does not prove He intended every person to attain faith and righteous action.
rows.anchor: ولكن لم قلتم إنها تدل على أنه تعالى أراد من الكل الإيمان والعمل الصالح

rows.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
rows.claim: Saʿīd ibn Jubayr reports that listeners asked Muhammad for stories after he recited Qur'an, so Sūrat Yūsuf was revealed; they then asked for hadith and reminders, followed by 39:23 and 57:16.
rows.anchor: روى سعيد بن جبير أنه تعالى لما أنزل القرآن على رسول الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qaṣaṣ originally means following one report or trace after another, as in following the infant's trace and retracing footprints.
rows.anchor: القصص اتباع الخبر بعضه بعضا وأصله في اللغة المتابعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qaṣaṣ may be a verbal noun meaning recounting; on this reading, the best quality is the story's eloquent, miraculous expression, unlike historical tellings.
rows.anchor: فإن حملناه على المصدر كان المعنى نقص عليك أحسن الاقتصاص

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qaṣaṣ may instead name what is recounted; then it is best for its lessons, wisdom, marvels, and signs absent from other stories.
rows.anchor: وإن حملناه على المفعول كان معنى كونه أحسن القصص لما فيه من العبر والنكت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One lesson is that no one can repel God's decree: if He decrees good for someone, all the world cannot prevent it.
rows.anchor: لا دافع لقضاء الله تعالى ولا مانع من قدر الله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The story teaches that envy brings abandonment and loss.
rows.anchor: دلالتها على أن الحسد سبب للخذلان والنقصان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: It also teaches that patience opens relief, as with both Jacob and Joseph.
rows.anchor: أن الصبر مفتاح الفرج كما في حق يعقوب عليه السلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Bi-mā awḥaynā means by Our revelation of this Qur'an if mā with the verb is treated as a verbal noun.
rows.anchor: فالمعنى بوحينا إليك هذا القرآن ، وهذا التقدير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The first reading of being among the heedless means Muhammad did not know Joseph's story before revelation; another takes it as his prior lack of knowledge of scripture and religion, as in 42:52.
rows.anchor: المراد أنه كان من الغافلين عن الدين والشريعة قبل ذلك

rows.speaker: صاحب الكشاف
rows.claim: The verse means: remember when Joseph said this; al-Kashshāf says Yūsuf is Hebrew because an Arabic form would be declinable absent another cause of diptosis.
rows.anchor: الصحيح أنه اسم عبراني

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some readers pronounce the sīn in Yūsuf with kasra and others with fatḥa; three such forms are also reported for Yūnus.
rows.anchor: بكسر السين { ويوسف } بفتحها

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: The Prophet says that when asked who is noble, one should answer Joseph son of Jacob, Isaac, and Abraham.
rows.anchor: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال : ( إذا قيل من الكريم

rows.speaker: ابن عامر
rows.claim: Ibn ʿĀmir opens the tāʾ in yā abat throughout the Qur'an; the others use kasra.
rows.anchor: قرأ ابن عامر { * يا أبت } بفتح التاء في جميع القرآن

rows.speaker: ثعلب وابن الأنباري
rows.claim: The open tāʾ derives from yā abatāh after dropping alif and hāʾ; the kasra derives from yā abī after dropping yāʾ, retaining its kasra, and adding pause hāʾ, later treated as part of the word.
rows.anchor: وهذا قول ثعلب وابن الأنباري

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Joseph's dream's eleven stars are his eleven brothers, sun and moon his parents, and their prostration means they humbled themselves and submitted to his authority.
rows.anchor: والسجود بتواضعهم له ودخولهم تحت أمره

rows.speaker: الفلاسفة
rows.claim: Philosophers who regard stars as living and rational cite their prostration here and the plural masculine verb for celestial bodies in 21:33.
rows.anchor: جماعة من الفلاسفة الذين يزعمون أن الكواكب أحياء ناطقة احتجوا بهذه الآية

rows.speaker: الواحدي
rows.claim: Al-Wāḥidī says that describing the stars as prostrating makes them seem rational, permitting a rational form of address, as with idols and the ant in 7:198 and 27:18.
rows.anchor: الواحدي : إنه تعالى لما وصفها بالسجود صارت كأنها تعقل

rows.speaker: القفال
rows.claim: Al-Qaffāl says the first seeing identifies the stars, sun, and moon, while the repeated seeing specifies that he saw them prostrating.
rows.anchor: قال القفال رحمه الله : ذكر الرؤية الأولى لتدل على أنه شاهد الكواكب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One explanation treats the wording as a question and answer: he said he saw the celestial bodies, then clarified how he saw them—as prostrating.
rows.anchor: فكأنه قيل له : كيف رأيت ؟ فقال : رأيتهم لي ساجدين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A further explanation assigns one occurrence to dream-seeing and the other to waking sight, but the author says it is too vague because it never says which is which.
rows.anchor: وهذا القائل لم يبين أن أيهما يحمل على الرؤيا وأيهما الرؤيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sun and moon are named after the stars to mark their greater honor; singling out honored figures similarly occurs in 2:98.
rows.anchor: أخرهما لفضلهما على الكواكب ، لأن التخصيص بالذكر يدل على مزيد الشرف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Prostration may be literal or mean humility, as in the poetic line about hills bowing to hooves; literal prostration is preferred because dreams can show it and nothing prevents it.
rows.anchor: كلاهما محتمل ، والأصل في الكلام حمله على حقيقته ولا مانع أن يرى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Joseph certainly had the dream as a child, but its exact date is known only through reports.
rows.anchor: لا شك أنه رآها حال الصغر ، فأما ذلك الزمان بعينه فلا يعلم إلا بالأخبار

rows.speaker: وهب
rows.claim: Wahb says that at seven Joseph dreamed of eleven upright staffs in a circle and a small staff leaping over and swallowing them; Jacob told him not to tell his brothers.
rows.anchor: قال وهب : رأى يوسف عليه السلام وهو ابن سبع سنين

rows.speaker: وهب
rows.claim: Wahb adds that at twelve Joseph saw sun, moon, and stars prostrating, then told Jacob, who warned him not to tell his brothers.
rows.anchor: ثم رأى وهو ابن ثنتي عشرة سنة الشمس والقمر والكواكب تسجد له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Reports place the interval between Joseph's dream and his brothers' arrival before him at forty or eighty years.
rows.anchor: كان بين رؤيا يوسف ومصير أخوته إليه أربعون سنة

rows.speaker: الحكماء
rows.claim: Philosophers say bad dreams are interpreted soon but good dreams much later: mercy delays knowledge of approaching evil to shorten grief and announces good early to extend joy.
rows.anchor: والسبب في ذلك أن رحمة الله تقتضي أن لا يحصل الإعلام بوصول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some identify the sun and moon as Joseph's father and maternal aunt because his mother had died and was absent in Egypt; the argument that a prophetic dream requires a living mother is weak because Joseph was not yet a prophet.
rows.anchor: لأن يوسف عليه السلام ما كان في ذلك الوقت من الأنبياء

rows.speaker: صاحب الكشاف
rows.claim: Al-Kashshāf reports that a Jew asked Muhammad for the stars' names; Gabriel supplied Jarbān, al-Ṭāriq, al-Dhayyāl, Qābis, ʿAmūdān, al-Fulayq, al-Muṣbiḥ, al-Ḍarūḥ, al-Fargh, Wathāb, and Dhū al-Katifayn, and the Jew affirmed them.
rows.anchor: جربان والطارق والذيال وقابس وعمودان والفليق والمصبح والضروح والفرغ ووثاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author notes that many of these names are absent from standard works describing constellations and leaves their reality to God.
rows.anchor: أن كثيرا من هذه الأسماء غير مذكور في الكتب المصنفة في صورة الكواكب

rows.speaker: حفص
rows.claim: Ḥafṣ reads yā bunayya with an open final yāʾ; the others read it with kasra.
rows.anchor: قرأ حفص { أو بنى } بفتح الياء والباقون بالكسر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jacob loved Joseph and Benjamin intensely; their jealousy was apparent, and Joseph's dream meant his family would submit to him, so Jacob warned him they would plot if told.
rows.anchor: فلما ذكر يوسف عليه السلام هذه الرؤيا وكان تأويلها أن إخوته وأبويه يخضعون له

rows.speaker: الواحدي
rows.claim: Al-Wāḥidī calls ruʾyā a verbal noun like bushrā and suqyā, later lexicalized for the thing seen in sleep.
rows.anchor: قال الواحدي : الرؤيا مصدر كالبشرى والسقيا والشورى

rows.speaker: صاحب الكشاف
rows.claim: Al-Kashshāf distinguishes ruʾyā for a dream from ruʾya for waking sight, differentiating the forms by feminine endings.
rows.anchor: الرؤيا بمعنى الرؤية إلا أنها مختصة بما كان منها في المنام دون اليقطة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other readings change the hamza to wāw or assimilate it, with the rāʾ read rounded or unrounded; the author calls these weak.
rows.anchor: وقرىء روياك بقلب الهمزة واوا وسمع الكسائي يقرأ رياك ورياك بالإدغام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In fayakīdū laka, the subjunctive follows an implicit an; it means that if Joseph tells them, they will plot against him.
rows.anchor: وهو منصوب بإضمار أن والمعنى إن قصصتها عليهم كادوك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The lām either reinforces the verbal connection, like naṣaḥtuka and naṣaḥtu laka, or attaches to plotting with the sense of plotting for you; scholars infer the brothers knew dream interpretation.
rows.anchor: قال أهل التحقيق : وهذا يدل على أنه قد كان لهم علم بتعبير الرؤيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jacob mentions Satan because any plot they undertook would be attributable to Satan, as in Moses' statement that this is Satan's work.
rows.anchor: والسبب في هذا الكلام أنهم لو أقدموا على الكيد لكان ذلك مضافا إلى الشيطان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: As God selected Joseph through this remarkable dream, He will select him for momentous affairs.
rows.anchor: وكما اجتباك بمثل هذه الرؤيا العظيمة الدالة على شرف وعز وكبر شأن

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjāj derives ijtabā from gathering or selecting something for oneself, as when water is gathered in a basin.
rows.anchor: قال الزجاج : الاجتباء مشتق من جبيت الشيء إذا خلصته لنفسك

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Ḥasan says God's selection means granting Joseph prophethood.
rows.anchor: فقال الحسن : يجتبيك ربك بالنبوة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Others understand selection as elevation and honor; the wording alone does not establish prophethood.
rows.anchor: المراد منه إعلاء الدرجة وتعظيم المرتبة فأما تعيين النبوة فلا دلالة في اللفظ عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Taʾwīl al-aḥādīth may mean interpreting people's dreams, whose outcome corresponds to what was seen; Joseph excelled in this art.
rows.anchor: المراد منه تعبير الرؤيا سماه تأويلا لأنه يؤل أمره إلى ما رآه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: It may mean interpreting God's books and traditions transmitted from earlier prophets, like scholars interpret scripture and prophetic reports.
rows.anchor: تأويل الأحاديث في كتب الله تعالى والأخبار المروية عن الأنبياء المتقدمين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Aḥādīth may mean events, whose outcomes return to God's power, creation, and wisdom; their interpretation is reasoning from created kinds to His attributes.
rows.anchor: ومآل الحوادث إلى قدرة الله تعالى وتكوينه وحكمته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If selection means prophethood, completion of blessing instead means worldly and afterlife felicity: family, servants, wealth, standing, praise, knowledge, virtue, and knowing God.
rows.anchor: يفسر إتمام النعمة ههنا بسعادات الدنيا وسعادات الآخرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If selection means elevated rank, completion means prophethood: only prophethood makes human blessing fully complete, and Abraham and Isaac were distinguished by it.
rows.anchor: فإن جميع مناصب الخلق دون منصب الرسالة ناقص بالنسبة إلى كمال النبوة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the prophethood reading, all Jacob's sons were prophets because the blessing is completed upon Jacob's family; the eleven stars represent exemplary people whose knowledge and religion guide the earth.
rows.anchor: لزم الحكم بأن أولاد يعقوب كلهم كانوا أنبياء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An objection asks how Jacob's sons could be prophets given their wrongdoing against Joseph.
rows.anchor: كيف يجوز أن يكونوا أنبياء وقد أقدموا على ما أقدموا عليه في حق يوسف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their wrongdoing happened before prophethood; the author's doctrine requires prophetic protection only once prophethood begins.
rows.anchor: ذاك وقع قبل النبوة ، وعندنا العصمة إنما تعتبر في وقت النبوة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another reading takes completion of blessing as rescue from trials, analogous to God saving Abraham from fire and Isaac from sacrifice.
rows.anchor: المراد من قوله : { ويتم نعمته عليك } خلاصه من المحن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A third reading is that God joined Joseph's worldly blessings of prophethood and kingship to the afterlife blessings of paradise.
rows.anchor: أن إتمام النعمة هو وصل نعمة الله عليه في الدنيا بنعم الآخرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author prefers completion as prophethood, the only complete human blessing; ʿAlīm points to God's knowledge of whom to choose, and Ḥakīm to His placing prophethood only in a pure soul.
rows.anchor: القول الصحيح هو الأول ، لأن النعمة التامة في حق البشر ليست إلا النبوة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An objection asks whether Jacob was certain of the promises: certainty seems incompatible with grief, fearing the brothers, or mentioning a wolf; uncertainty seems incompatible with his firm prediction.
rows.anchor: فكيف حزن على يوسف عليه السلام ، وكيف جاز أن يشتبه عليه أن الذئب أكله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jacob's promise may have been conditional on the brothers not plotting, since he had just warned Joseph of their scheme.
rows.anchor: لا يبعد أن يكون قوله : { وكذالك يجتبيك ربك } مشروطا بأن لا يكيدوه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Even knowing Joseph would attain high rank, Jacob could fear the severe ordeals before eventual deliverance; the wolf warning urged care though he knew the wolf would not reach Joseph.
rows.anchor: لا يمتنع أن يقع في المضايق الشديدة ثم يتخلص منها ويصل إلى تلك المناصب

rows.speaker: صاحب الكشاف
rows.claim: Al-Kashshāf names Joseph's siblings: Yehuda, Ruben, Simeon, Levi, Rabūlūn, Yashjar, Dina, Dan, Naphtali, Gad, and Asher; Leah bore the first seven, handmaids Zilpah and Bilhah the next four, while Rachel later bore Benjamin and Joseph.
rows.anchor: صاحب ( الكشاف ) أسماء إخوة يوسف : يهودا

rows.speaker: ابن كثير
rows.claim: Ibn Kathīr reads the word as singular āyah, tying it to Joseph's affair; the others read plural āyāt because his story contains many signs, each a sign in itself.
rows.anchor: قرأ ابن كثير آية بغير ألف حمله على شأن يوسف والباقون { ءايات }

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās reports a Jewish scholar heard Muhammad recite Joseph's story as in the Torah, returned with others to listen, and they asked who taught him; God revealed that the story contains signs for questioners.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس دخل حبر من اليهود على النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم فسمع منه قراءة يوسف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author finds that report unlikely: the verse places signs in Joseph's story, whereas the report makes Muhammad's uninstructed knowledge the sign, which is a different claim.
rows.anchor: لأن المفهوم من الآية أن في واقعة يوسف آيات للسائلين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A second explanation addresses Meccans hostile to the Prophet: Joseph's brothers harmed him from envy, yet God ultimately empowered him, warning listeners against envy.
rows.anchor: ومثل هذه الواقعة إذا سمعها العاقل كانت زجرا له عن الإقدام على الحسد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A third explanation compares Joseph's dream taking eighty years to come true with any delay in Muhammad's promised victory, which would not make him false.
rows.anchor: وقع ذلك التعبير ودخل في الوجود بعد ثمانين سنة فكذلك أن الله تعالى لما وعد محمدا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A fourth explanation says enemies could not undo God's promise to Joseph, just as unbelievers cannot undo God's promise to raise Muhammad's rank.
rows.anchor: فكذلك واقعة محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم فإن الله لما ضمن له إعلاء الدرجة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The story offers many signs to anyone who asks, as does the provision described as four days in 41:10.
rows.anchor: { فى أربعة أيام سواء للسائلين }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The lām in layūsuf is an emphatic introductory particle; Benjamin is called Joseph's brother because they shared a mother.
rows.anchor: اللام لام الابتداء ، وفيها تأكيد وتحقيق لمضمون الجملة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ʿUṣba means a group of ten or more, by some accounts up to forty, called so because they reinforce one another's affairs.
rows.anchor: والعصبة والعصابة العشرة فصاعدا ، وقيل إلى الأربعين سموا بذلك

rows.speaker: علي
rows.claim: ʿAlī is reported to read wa-naḥnu ʿuṣbatan in the accusative, meaning that they come together as a group.
rows.anchor: علي عليه السلام أنه قرأ { ونحن عصبة } بالنصب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They resented Jacob's preference because they were older, stronger and more useful in managing his needs, and better at warding off harm and securing benefits.
rows.anchor: أنهم كانوا أكبر سنا منهما . وثانيها : أنهم كانوا أكثر قوة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their charge that Jacob was in obvious error means, in their view, that his preference was conspicuously unfair and misguided.
rows.anchor: يعني هذا حيف ظاهر وضلال بين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jacob is excused for unequal affection because affection is beyond human control; he did not favor them in an action within his power.
rows.anchor: والمحبة ليست في وسع البشر فكان معذورا فيه ولا يلحقه بسبب ذلك لوم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The brothers believed Jacob was a true prophet but thought prophets might make particular decisions by independent judgment; they thought their age, reason, competence, and service justified preference.
rows.anchor: أنهم كانوا مؤمنين بنبوة أبيهم مقرين بكونه رسولا حقا من عند الله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jacob could answer that increased affection is involuntary; his greater care may also reflect that Joseph and Benjamin were young or motherless, showed promise, or served him especially well.
rows.anchor: أن أمهما ماتت وهما صغار . وثانيها : لأنه كان يرى فيه من آثار الرشد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because the dispute involved judgment mixed with natural affection, it does not impugn either side's religion or character.
rows.anchor: هذه المسألة كانت اجتهادية ، وكانت مخلوطة بميل النفس وموجبات الفطرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their accusation of obvious error means Jacob neglected worldly interests, not that he departed from guidance or right belief.
rows.anchor: المراد منه الضلال عن رعاية المصالح في الدنيا لا البعد عن طريق الرشد والصواب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An objection says their envy led to grave sins—lying, consigning Joseph to slavery, separating him from Jacob, and causing their father's lasting grief—undermining prophetic impeccability.
rows.anchor: والحسد من أمهات الكبائر ، لا سيما وقد أقدموا على الكذب بسبب ذلك الحسد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author replies that prophetic impeccability is required during prophethood, not before it.
rows.anchor: الأمر كما ذكرتم ، إلا أن المعتبر عندنا عصمة الأنبياء عليهم السلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: At the height of envy they resolved to remove Joseph by killing or exiling him, the worst harm they could devise, so their father's attention would turn to them.
rows.anchor: لا يحصل إلا بأحد طريقين : القتل أو التغريب إلى أرض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their claim that they would become righteous afterward may mean they would repent of the major sin they planned.
rows.anchor: إذا فعلنا ذلك تبنا إلى الله ونصير من القوم الصالحين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, righteous may mean their situation with their father would improve and he would devote himself to them.
rows.anchor: المعنى يصلح شأنكم عند أبيكم ويصير أبوكم محبا لكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A third reading is that removing their emotional distress would let them focus on putting their affairs in order.
rows.anchor: فإذا زالت هذه الوحشة تفرغتم لإصلاح مهماتكم

rows.speaker: وهب
rows.claim: Wahb identifies the brother who proposed killing Joseph as Simeon; Muqātil instead identifies Ruben.
rows.anchor: وهب : إنه شمعون ، وقال مقاتل : روبيل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author rejects the claim that they were immature children: Jacob would not send children without a responsible escort, and their promise of later reform implies they were culpable.
rows.anchor: لا يكونون صالحين ، وذلك ينافي كونهم من الصبيان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling the plot a minor sin is also untenable: harming their prophetic father, lying, and trying to destroy their young brother are major sins.
rows.anchor: والكذب معه والسعي في إهلاك الأخ الصغير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The correct answer is that the brothers were not prophets, or that this event occurred before their prophethood.
rows.anchor: يقال : إنهم ما كانوا أنبياء ، وإن كانوا أنبياء إلا أن هذه الواقعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The one who stopped the murder was either Ruben, Joseph's maternal cousin and his kindest brother, or Yehuda, oldest in judgment, merit, and age.
rows.anchor: قيل إنه كان روبيل وكان ابن خالة يوسف وكان أحسنهم رأيا فيه

rows.speaker: نافع
rows.claim: Nāfiʿ reads ghiyābat in the two occurrences as plural, for the well has several corners; the singular names the single hidden place and is more precise.
rows.anchor: قرأ نافع { فى * غيابة الجب } على الجمع في الحرفين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ghiyāba is anything concealing something, here the unseen dark bottom of the well; jubb is an unlined well, merely excavated.
rows.anchor: الغيابة كل ما غيب شيئا وستره ، فغيابة الجب غوره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The word ghiyāba specifies a dark concealed spot so passersby would not see Joseph, since the well might otherwise have visible places.
rows.anchor: أشار بطرحه في موضع مظلم من الجب لا يلحقه نظر الناظرين

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatāda locates the well in Jerusalem; Wahb places it in Jordan, while Muqātil says three farsakhs from Jacob's home.
rows.anchor: قال قتادة : هو بئر ببيت المقدس ، وقال وهب : هو بأرض الأردن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They chose a well frequented by caravans because a traveler would find Joseph and rescue him, making the plan less likely to kill him.
rows.anchor: وإذا وردوها شاهدوا ذلك الإنسان فيها ، وإذا شاهدوه أخرجوه وذهبوا به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Iltqāṭ means picking something up from the road, as in the related words for found property and an abandoned child; a caravan is a traveling group.
rows.anchor: الالتقاط تناول الشيء من الطريق ، ومنه : اللقطة واللقيط

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Ḥasan reads taltaqiṭhu with feminine tāʾ because some of a caravan is itself a caravan by meaning.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الحسن { * تلتقطه } بالتاء على المعنى ، لأن بعض السيارة أيضا سيارة

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās explains al-sayyāra as passersby; the speaker's if you must act hints that doing nothing would be better, like the limit in 16:126.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس : يريد المارة وقوله : { السيارة إن كنتم فاعلين }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jacob's sons' question shows he already feared them with respect to Joseph.
rows.anchor: هذا الكلام يدل على أن يعقوب عليه السلام كان يخافهم على يوسف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After fixing their plan, they pretended deep love and concern, citing their usual herding trips; Jacob wanted to please Joseph, trusted them, and sent him.
rows.anchor: أظهروا عند أبيهم أنهم في غاية المحبة ليوسف وفي غاية الشفقة عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The readings of la taʾmannā separate the two nūns or assimilate them, with or without ishmaam; the meaning is that Jacob should trust them to love and care for Joseph.
rows.anchor: { لا تأمنا } قرىء بإظهار النونين وبالإدغام بإشمام وبغير إشمام

rows.speaker: ابن كثير
rows.claim: Ibn Kathīr reads nartaʿ with nūn and kasra, from grazing: the brothers mean they will tend their livestock, while play is attributed to Joseph as a child.
rows.anchor: قرأ ابن كثير : بالنون ، وبكسر عين نرتع من الارتعاء

rows.speaker: نافع
rows.claim: Nāfiʿ reads both verbs with yāʾ and kasra in yartaʿ, attributing grazing to Joseph so he can learn to tend livestock, as well as play.
rows.anchor: قرأ نافع : كلاهما بالياء وكسر العين من يرتع أضاف الارتعاء إلى يوسف

rows.speaker: أبو عمرو وابن عامر
rows.claim: Abū ʿAmr and Ibn ʿĀmir read nartaʿ and nalʿab with nūn and jussive verbs; Ibn al-Aʿrābī defines ratʿ as eating greedily, while others say abundance or fertility.
rows.anchor: قرأ أبو عمرو وابن عامر { * نرتع } بالنون وجزم العين ومثله نلعب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Play may mean permitted recreation; Muhammad's remark to Jābir about a wife playing with him is cited as precedent.
rows.anchor: كما روي عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه قال لجابر : ( فهلا بكرا تلاعبها وتلاعبك )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their play may have been racing to learn warfare, supported by their later statement that they went to race; it was called play because of its outward form.
rows.anchor: كان لعبهم الاستباق ، والغرض منه تعلم المحاربة والمقاتلة مع الكفار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The brothers regularly went away to graze, so they asked Jacob to let Joseph accompany them.
rows.anchor: وكانت عادتهم أن يغيبوا عنه مدة إلى الرعي فسألوه أن يرسله معهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jacob wanted to please Joseph, was deceived by the brothers’ words, and sent Joseph with them.
rows.anchor: يحب تطييب قلب يوسف فاغتر بقولهم وأرسله معهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jacob gives two excuses: separation from Joseph grieves him because he cannot bear an hour apart, and he fears a wolf may attack while the brothers are distracted.
rows.anchor: أن ذهابهم به ومفارقتهم إياه مما يحزنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some say Jacob had dreamed a wolf attacked Joseph, so he warned them and effectively suggested the pretext; a proverb says misfortune is bound to one's words.
rows.anchor: إنه رأى في النوم أن الذئب شد على يوسف ، فكان يحذره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Others say wolves were numerous in their territory.
rows.anchor: الذئاب كانت في أراضيهم كثيرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-dhiʾb is read with the original hamza or with tafkhīm; its root is also linked to wind coming from every direction.
rows.anchor: وقرىء { الذئب } بالهمز على الأصل

rows.speaker: صاحب الكشاف
rows.claim: The lām in laʾin reinforces the entailment between condition and consequence, or marks an omitted oath: by God, if the wolf eats him, we will be losers.
rows.anchor: هذه اللام تدل على إضمار القسم تقديره : والله لئن أكله الذئب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wāw in wa-naḥnu ʿuṣba is circumstantial: they swear while being a ten-man band able to handle crises.
rows.anchor: أنها واو الحال حلفوا لئن حصل ما خافه من خطف الذئب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Losers may mean weak and helpless, as in 23:34.
rows.anchor: خاسرون أي هالكون ضعفا وعجزا ، ونظيره قوله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, they would deserve to be condemned and cursed as destroyers of their brother.
rows.anchor: مستحقين لأن يدعى عليهم بالخسارة والدمار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They may mean that failure to protect Joseph would also mean losing their livestock.
rows.anchor: المعنى أنا إن لم نقدر على حفظ أخينا فقد هلكت مواشينا وخسرناها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They may mean that neglecting Joseph would nullify all the labor they had performed in Jacob's service for his praise and prayers.
rows.anchor: لو قصرنا في هذه الخدمة فقد أحبطنا كل تلك الأعمال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They ignore Jacob's first excuse because their resentment arose from his love for Joseph; they deliberately passed over that point.
rows.anchor: أن حقدهم وغيظهم كان بسبب العذر الأول ، وهو شدة حبه له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse omits two things: Jacob's permission and sending Joseph with them, then the response to when they took him, namely that they put him in the well.
rows.anchor: فأذن له وأرسله معهم ثم يتصل به قوله

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddī recounts that the brothers beat Joseph almost to death; Yehuda invoked their pledge, and they stripped his shirt to fake wolf's blood before lowering him into the well.
rows.anchor: قال السدي : إن يوسف عليه السلام لما برز مع إخوته

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: In al-Suddī's account Joseph clung halfway down; they mocked him to summon the stars, dropped him into water, and he climbed onto a rock crying; they tried to crush him, but Yehuda stopped them and brought food.
rows.anchor: حتى إذا بلغ نصفها ألقوه ليموت ، وكان في البئر ماء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report gives Joseph's prayer in the well: O witness who is not absent, near who is not far, victorious who cannot be overcome, make me a way out.
rows.anchor: روي أنه عليه السلام لما ألقي في الجب قال يا شاهدا غير غائب . ويا قريبا غير بعيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another report says Gabriel clothed Abraham in silk from paradise in the fire; Abraham passed it to Isaac, then Jacob kept it as Joseph's amulet, and Gabriel dressed Joseph with it in the well.
rows.anchor: وروي أن إبراهيم عليه السلام لما ألقي في النار جرد عن ثيابه فجاءه جبريل عليه السلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The first view takes God's revelation to Joseph as prophethood, held by many investigators; they disagree whether he was seventeen or a child whose mind God completed for revelation, like Jesus.
rows.anchor: المراد منه الوحي والنبوة والرسالة وهذا قول طائفة عظيمة من المحققين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A second view takes the revelation as inspiration, like God's inspiration to Moses' mother and the bees.
rows.anchor: كما في قوله تعالى : { وأوحينا إلى أم موسى }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The first interpretation is preferable because revelation ordinarily means prophethood.
rows.anchor: لأن الظاهر من الوحي ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Though no one was then present to receive a message, God could confer revelation and defer the mission; early revelation comforted Joseph and eased his fear.
rows.anchor: تقديم الوحي تأنيسه وتسكين نفسه وإزالة الغم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One reading of they do not perceive is that Joseph would later tell his brothers what they did while they did not recognize him, strengthening him with promise of release and eventual power over them.
rows.anchor: إنك لتخبرن إخوتك بصنيعهم بعد هذا اليوم وهم لا يشعرون في ذلك الوقت إنك يوسف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another reading is that the brothers did not know revelation had come to Joseph in the well; concealment prevented them from becoming still more jealous and killing him.
rows.anchor: والفائدة في إخفاء نزول ذلك الوحي عنهم أنهم لو عرفوه فربما ازداد حسدهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report says that when the brothers later came to buy grain, Joseph recognized them; the divining cup seemed to tell him they had thrown their paternal brother in a well and blamed a wolf.
rows.anchor: إنه ليخبرني هذا الجام أنه كان لكم أخ من أبيكم

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: A sayyāra is a traveling party; Ibn ʿAbbās says travelers from Midian to Egypt lost their way, reached Joseph's remote well, and its water became fresh after he was put in it.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس : جاءت سيارة أي قوم يسيرون من مدين إلى مصر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The water drawer was Mālik ibn Dhuʿar al-Khuzāʿī, sent to find water for the group.
rows.anchor: يقال له : مالك بن ذعر الخزاعي ليطلب لهم الماء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wāрид is the person who goes to the water to draw it for the party.
rows.anchor: والوارد الذي يرد الماء ليستقي القوم

rows.speaker: عامة أهل اللغة
rows.claim: Most linguists distinguish adlā, lowering a bucket into a well, from dalā, pulling it out; the verbal forms mark lowering versus drawing.
rows.anchor: عن عامة أهل اللغة أنه يقال : أدلى دلوه إذا أرسلها في البئر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The narrative omits that Joseph appeared: he caught the rope as the water drawer lowered the bucket, and the man called out at the sight of the beautiful boy.
rows.anchor: والتقدير : فظهر يوسف قال المفسرون : لما أدلى الوارد دلوه

rows.speaker: عاصم وحمزة والكسائي
rows.claim: ʿĀṣim, Ḥamza, and al-Kisāʾī read yā bushrā without alif and with still yāʾ; the others read yā bushrāya with alif and open yāʾ.
rows.anchor: قرأ عاصم وحمزة والكسائي { بشرى } بغير الألف وبسكون الياء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One view treats bushrā as an exclamation at good news, like yā ʿajabā; Zajjāj says addressing an inanimate thing alerts hearers and emphasizes the event.
rows.anchor: قال الزجاج : معنى النداء في هذه الأشياء التي لا تجيب تنبيه المخاطبين

rows.speaker: أبو علي
rows.claim: Abū ʿAlī explains it as saying, O good news, this is your moment; if you could speak, I would call you and command you to come.
rows.anchor: قال أبو علي : كأنه يقول : يا أيتها البشرى هذا الوقت وقتك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The finders rejoiced because they found a strikingly handsome boy whom they expected to sell for a high price and profit from.
rows.anchor: وقالوا : نبيعه بثمن عظيم ويصير ذلك سببا لحصول الغنى

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddī says the caller addressed a companion named Bushrā, like calling someone Zayd; al-Aʿmash says Bushrā was a woman's name.
rows.anchor: الذي ذكره السدي أن الذي نادى صاحبه

rows.speaker: أبو علي الفارسي
rows.claim: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī says if bushrā means good news, it may be nominative as a specific vocative or accusative as a generic one, like yā ḥasratan in 36:30.
rows.anchor: أبو علي الفارسي : إن جعلنا البشرى اسما للبشارة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun in asarrūhu may mean the water drawer and companions, who hid the boy from the caravan to avoid sharing and claimed they had been entrusted with him to sell.
rows.anchor: أنه عائد إلى الوارد وأصحابه أخفوا من الرفقة أنهم وجدوه في الجب

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās instead says Joseph's brothers hid that he was their brother and called him an escaped slave; Joseph went along because they threatened him in Hebrew.
rows.anchor: نقل عن ابن عباس أنه قال : { وأسروه } يعني : إخوة يوسف أسروا شأنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author prefers the water party as the pronoun's referent because they hid him precisely while treating him as merchandise; that fits the context better than the brothers' account.
rows.anchor: والأول أولى لأن قوله : { وأسروه بضاعة } يدل على أن المراد

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjāj parses bidaʿa as an accusative circumstantial expression: they concealed him while treating him as merchandise.
rows.anchor: قال الزجاج : وبضاعة منصوبة على الحال كأنه قال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's knowledge frames the irony: the brothers' effort to prevent Joseph's dream caused his ordeal, but God made it the path to Egypt, kingship, and fulfillment of the dream.
rows.anchor: فكان العمل الذي عمله الأعداء في دفعه عن ذلك المطلوب

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says the brothers returned after three days, found Joseph gone, tracked down the caravan, claimed he was their runaway slave, and sold him to them; the pronoun also refers to them in the next clause.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما : إن إخوة يوسف لما طرحوا يوسف

rows.speaker: محمد بن إسحاق
rows.claim: Muḥammad ibn Isḥāq says the sellers may have been Joseph's brothers or the caravan members who found him; God knows which.
rows.anchor: وقال محمد بن إسحاق : ربك أعلم أإخوته باعوه أم السيارة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another interpretation gives shara as ordinary purchase: the caravan bought Joseph while feigning indifference to negotiate a low price, perhaps suspecting the brothers' lie or recognizing his lineage and fearing the consequences.
rows.anchor: المراد من الشراء نفس الشراء ، والمعنى أن القوم اشتروه

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujāhid says the buyers told one another to secure Joseph so he would not run away.
rows.anchor: قال مجاهد : وكانوا يقولون استوثقوا منه لئلا يأبق

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās interprets bakhs as unlawful because a free person's price is forbidden; he says elsewhere in the Qur'an it means decrease, but here it means unlawful.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس : يريد حراما لأن ثمن الحر حرام

rows.speaker: الواحدي
rows.claim: Al-Wāḥidī explains unlawful price as deficient in blessing.
rows.anchor: قال الواحدي سموا الحرام بخسا لأنه ناقص البركة

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatāda reads bakhs as injustice, which entails reduction.
rows.anchor: وقال قتادة : بخس ظلم والظلم نقصان

rows.speaker: عكرمة والشعبي
rows.claim: ʿIkrima and al-Shaʿbī take bakhs to mean little; another view says it was plainly below value, or that the coins were debased and underweight.
rows.anchor: وقال عكرمة والشعبي قليل وقيل : ناقص عن القيمة نقصانا ظاهرا

rows.speaker: الواحدي
rows.claim: Al-Wāḥidī concludes that under all these readings bakhs is a verbal noun used as a noun, meaning a diminished or undervalued price.
rows.anchor: وعلى الأقوال كلها ، فالبخس مصدر وضع موضع الاسم
